title: Engineering All-Hands - 2026-04-01
body:
Attendees: eng-platform-engineering, serving-runtime, SRE, developer-experience, product-hosted-api (approx 70 people on the call)

Purpose: weekly org-wide sync to align on platform priorities, surface outages/risk, and share cross-team progress. Shorter format this week (45m).

Agenda:
- Quick metrics & health (5m)
- Team highlights (20m)
- Incident / SLO updates (5m)
- Upcoming launches and rollouts (10m)
- Action items / blockers (5m)

1) Quick metrics & health
- Production p99 gen latency (global): 210ms (rolling 7d) - slight increase vs last week (190ms).
- Hosted API overall availability: 99.96% (last 7d). One brief region outage (us-west-2 eq) caused 30m of degraded latency during peak.
- Dedicated cluster utilization: avg 72% across reserved pools; one customer cluster trending to 92% during afternoon spikes (see INFRA-4823).
- Token cost guidance: optimized kernel rollout expected to reduce GPU token cost ~6-9% for medium-length sequences (benchmark set v3).

Notes: p99 increase traced to a regression in batching heuristics for short requests (sub-32 token). Diego and serving-runtime have a fix (PR #3421) queued for canary.

2) Team highlights
- Serving Runtime (Diego)
  - Rolling canary of kernel selection changes started yesterday across canary pool. Initial telemetry looks good for long-context models; short-context requests show the batching regression mentioned above.
  - PRs: github:.../serving-runtime#3421 (batching heuristics fix) - target canary promotion Thursday if no regression.
  - Next: begin safe-quantization experiments on metal-optimized kernels (internal perf harness).

- Platform Engineering (Maya)
  - Autoscaler tuning: deployed a bump to initial pod capacity thresholds for Dedicated for one high-util customer to reduce cold-start tail latency. Monitoring for side effects.
  - Landed API change to expose per-route cost-breakdown in analytics pipeline; SDK change coming next sprint.
  - Working with SRE to codify region-failover playbooks for customer-facing incidents.

- Site Reliability (Rina)
  - Incident postmortem (us-west-2): root cause was an autoscaler misconfiguration + a noisy neighbor GPU job. Postmortem draft uploaded to Confluence (linked). Action: enforce per-tenant scheduling constraints for Dedicated.
  - SLO calibration: proposing p99 target recalc for Hosted API + separate SLOs for short vs long requests to reflect different queuing profiles.

- Developer Experience (Aisha)
  - Console: new latency breakdown charts are in internal beta; requesting eng feedback on visual affordances (esp. prefix vs generation time).
  - Quickstart templates updated with Dedicated example for XGBoost workload (customer ask).

- Product / Hosted API (Liam)
  - Rollout plan for include-function-calls flag across hosted customers: staged rollout beginning 2026-04-10 with opt-out for early customers.
  - Billing: validation of unit accounting for streaming responses completed; finance sees expected delta within 0.3%.

3) Incident / SLO updates
- Action: Rina to finalize postmortem and run a cross-team dry-run of the failover playbook by 2026-04-09. (Owner: Rina Sato, due 2026-04-09)
- Action: Diego to promote batching fix to canary and collect telemetry across short/medium-length requests by 2026-04-03. (Owner: Diego Morales, due 2026-04-03)

4) Upcoming launches and rollouts
- Kernel selection safe rollout: staging -> canary -> full by 2026-04-15 (pending canary stability). Primary goal: reduce average token cost and improve long-context perf.
- Dedicated autoscaler policy changes targeted for customers with high spike patterns - pilot with Customer A next week.
- Console latency breakdown public beta: 2026-04-12. Teams to provide final UI feedback by 2026-04-08.

5) Decisions / discussions
- Decision: split Hosted API p99 SLO into two buckets (short requests < 64 tokens, long requests >= 64 tokens). This is to provide clearer SLA commitments and to drive targeted optimization. (Decision Owner: SRE/Product)
- Discussion: evaluate whether prefix caching TTL should be per-tenant or global. Action: platform to prototype per-tenant TTL config (Owner: Maya, due 2026-04-20).

6) Action items (summary)
- Diego Morales: promote batching heuristics fix to canary, collect metrics (due 2026-04-03).
- Rina Sato: finalize US-WEST-2 postmortem + run failover dry-run (due 2026-04-09).
- Maya Patel: prototype per-tenant prefix cache TTL config and share design doc (linked) (due 2026-04-20).
- Aisha Khan: gather eng feedback on console latency charts; finalize beta sign-up list (due 2026-04-08).
- Liam O'Connor: finalize rollout schedule for include-function-calls flag and coordinate customer comms (due 2026-04-07).

Open questions / notes to follow up:
- Need better heatmap visibility for short request queuing - propose a lightweight agent to sample queue lengths at ingress. (SRE/Serving to prototype)
- Confirm whether Dedicated reserved capacity metrics should report per-tenant effective headroom (yes, product wants this).

Meeting notes / miscellaneous:
- Quick kudos: platform-engineering on landing per-route cost breakdown; great cross-team collaboration.
- Reminder: engineering all-hands cadence stays weekly; next meeting 2026-04-08.

Attachments / referenced docs:
- Confluence postmortem draft: https://confluence.redwood/ENG/postmortem/us-west-2-2026-03-30
- Kernel rollout RFC: https://confluence.redwood/ENG/rfcs/kernel-selection-rollout-2026
- PR (batching fix): github:redwood-inference/serving-runtime#3421
- JIRA: INFRA-4823 (Dedicated cluster autoscaler), SRV-5102 (SLO proposal)

Notes-to-self / working thoughts (informal):
- Consider adding a short internal runbook card for devs to understand when to file a dedicated capacity scaling request.
- Track correlation of p99 blips with high metadata-access patterns (possible KV cache thrash).

-- end of notes --
